text:
Ethan: hi folks, new hire here. On macOS using company wg profile (split-tunnel). When I `curl internal-api.redwood` I get the public site instead of the internal LB. hostname resolves to 10.4.33.12 in our inventory but my machine gets 34.125.10.11 (public). anyone seen DNS policy vs split-tunnel issues?
Sophie: welcome! likely your DNS is still pointing at home ISP resolver for that query. with split-tunnel we push internal DNS via the wg interface but macOS can be finicky if the service order puts WiFi DNS first. can you paste `scutil --dns` output?
Ethan: pasted minimal bits:
```
resolver #1
  search domain[0] : redwood.internal
  nameserver[0] : 192.168.0.1
resolver #2
  domain   : 10.in-addr.arpa
  nameserver[0] : 10.4.10.2
```
Ethan: so the wg DNS 10.4.10.2 is listed but resolver #1 still points to my router.
it-support: macOS uses per-interface resolvers. Sometimes the user network (en0) resolver is preferred over virtual interfaces. two quick workarounds: (1) use `dig @10.4.10.2 internal-api.redwood` to confirm internal answer; (2) use `sudo networksetup -setdnsservers Wi-Fi 10.4.10.2` temporarily (requires admin) or (3) use SSH SOCKS via bastion `ssh -D 1080 bastionsvc@bastion.redwood` and point browser/docker to the SOCKS proxy.
Ethan: `dig @10.4.10.2 internal-api.redwood` returns 10.4.33.12 as expected. changing Wi-Fi DNS to 10.4.10.2 fixes browser but I lose split-tunnel behavior for other sites.
Sophie: that's expected. We usually tag complex-macos clients for `dns-priority-fix` (ticket ONB-5234) and push a small resolver config that ensures wg interface DNS is in system resolver order. For immediate access the SSH SOCKS trick is least intrusive.
eng-oncall-bot: Tip: if you rely on local hostnames often, set up /etc/hosts entries for a few critical services while we patch client profiles.
Ethan: thanks — opened ONB-5234 and used the ssh -D workaround to continue. appreciate the quick help!
it-support: welcome to the team Ethan, ping me if you want us to apply the dns-priority-fix to your account.
